title: Week 1: Nature and practical studio: Observation and inference; Square fold
objectives: Apply and explain nature and practical studio: observation and inference; square fold using the specified independent and transfer tasks.
entry_evidence: Describe an observation separately from an inference and follow one safe ordinary-paper procedure.

steps.instruction:
Use 30 minutes of short nature observations/analysis and 30 minutes of actual ordinary-paper work. An adult prepares the familiar accessible setting. Direct observation can use an available sensory channel: an already familiar safe ambient sound or the surface of a clean familiar natural-material object, without recording or identifying a species. Adapt the question to sequence, pattern, comparison or uncertainty and label the modality. Do not call an adult's description the learner's direct sensory observation. If no suitable direct route is available, use an explicitly invented model: 'Site A shows one branching shape, two visible edges and an obscured base.' That supports interpretation, not actual nature observation. No collection or unknown-object handling. Stop discomfort, strain or unsafe improvisation.
Entry check: ask the learner to demonstrate the stated prerequisite with a fresh example. If missing, teach that skill first; do not treat age or an earlier week number as evidence of readiness.
materials: Paper, pencil or accessible response tool
Adult packet kept separate from independent work
Ordinary whole paper sheets and pencil; optional accessible ruler and familiar books. Adult-selected familiar viewing place; no collection or handling of unknown objects.
